breakthrough: Software rewards can encourage outcomes beyond screen engagement
lane: Rewards, motivation, progression, and value exchange
outcome: Connect verified beneficial actions to digital progression and community recognition

phases.name: Phase 1 - Build the Real World Impact Core

subphases.name: 1.1 Real World Impact Domain Model and State Plane
work: Define typed entities, capabilities, jobs, events, state transitions, and outputs required to connect verified beneficial actions to digital progression and community recognition, with explicit versions and validation at every boundary.

Implement an owned persistent state layer optimized for rewards, achievements, quests, loyalty, motivation, progression, anti-exploitation, and community challenges; include snapshots or event history when state changes over time.
Expose create, query, update, subscribe, and delete operations through local APIs plus an SDK that never requires private cross-runtime imports.

subphases.name: 1.2 Real World Impact Execution Runtime
work: Build resumable workers and state machines that perform the core operation: connect verified beneficial actions to digital progression and community recognition.
Add cancellation, idempotency, bounded retries, timeouts, quotas, sandbox limits, and deterministic recovery from partial failure.
Create a local simulator that can replay success, malformed inputs, disconnection, overload, provider loss, and restart recovery.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Make Real World Impact Adaptive and Usable

subphases.name: 2.1 Real World Impact Decision and Learning Engine
work: Implement scoring, planning, prediction, search, or optimization using behavior modeling, reinforcement signals, game theory, anomaly detection, and adaptive difficulty.
Create feedback signals from task outcomes and user corrections; update tunable behavior without silently changing hard safety limits.
Return confidence, alternatives, bottlenecks, and a concise machine-readable explanation for every important automated choice.

subphases.name: 2.2 Real World Impact Interaction Surface
work: Build the primary experience in the reward forge, progression map, challenge studio, and motivation simulator, including live state, controls, errors, and recovery actions.
Add a CLI and typed client library so humans, agents, games, and third-party applications can operate the capability directly.
Stream progress and intermediate artifacts in real time so long operations remain inspectable, interruptible, and steerable.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Scale Real World Impact into a Breakthrough Product

subphases.name: 3.1 Real World Impact Offline, Edge, and Cloud Mesh
work: Implement local-only, hybrid, and cloud execution with explicit capability discovery and graceful behavior when optional peers disappear.
Add conflict-safe synchronization, workload placement, caching, backpressure, and failover across devices or nodes where the feature benefits from distribution.
Benchmark latency, throughput, memory, energy, network transfer, and cost; make the scheduler choose the best execution mode from measured constraints.

subphases.name: 3.2 Real World Impact Signature Breakthrough
work: Implement the differentiating behavior: Software rewards can encourage outcomes beyond screen engagement. Ship it as an opt-in executable mode, not a mockup.
Run adversarial, load, privacy, misuse, degraded-network, and recovery tests against the novel behavior; block unsafe automatic actions.
Package the feature as an independently installable capability with a live demo, sample integration, metrics endpoint, and rollback-safe release artifact.

title: Real-World Impact Rewards
